source: Statistics South Africa, National Household Travel Survey (NHTS) 2020
hash: not computed (public-use CC-BY per DataFirst); files ARE locally readable this session, verified live
geography: Province variable (Pr_code) confirmed present in the linked nhts-2020-geog.dta file (not currently joined by notebook 02); NHTS 2020 is a nationally-designed benchmark survey. Not independently re-tabulated by province this pass -- confirmed available, not confirmed as-tabulated.
age_universe: CONFIRMED, quantified live (this pass): traveller ages range 15-89, 0.41% aged 65+, none under 15. Filtering to working-age (15-64) moves the mean daily cost from R20.96 to R21.03 -- negligible on its own, dwarfed by the missingness finding below.
labour_market_universe: Job seekers who travelled while looking for work (Q47Travlooking==Yes), a narrower population than the expanded labour force -- NOT the same universe as discouraged_share/long_term_share
denominator: Numerator: mean daily cost over 4,655 travellers. Denominator: median monthly wage (Q410Salary/21.7) over ~20,867 respondents with a valid wage AND pay period -- a GENERAL population wage benchmark, not a job-seeker-specific one (job seekers have no wage by construction)
conditioning_event: Numerator conditions on Q47Travlooking==Yes, a single reported travel day; the cost is for that day only, not a monthly or per-trip average
weights: NHTS person-level Weight, applied to the cost side and the wage side independently (not jointly)
missingness_treatment: QUANTIFIED LIVE (this pass), not a minor footnote: 2,247 of 4,655 travellers (48.3%) have BOTH their first-travel-mode field (Q429bMode1Trv) AND its cost field (Q429b3Cost1) coded 'Unspecified' -- the whole first-mode sub-block is unanswered, not a legitimate zero (Q47Travlooking=Yes confirms they did travel). The current code treats this half of the sample as R0 transport cost. Only 6 of 4,655 have a real Mode1Trv with an Unspecified Cost1 (true cost-only missingness) -- the other 2,241 are a mode-and-cost joint non-response. Slots 2-4 (Cost2/3/4) being 'Unspecified' for the vast majority is separately normal and expected (almost everyone uses exactly one travel mode).
units: ratio of a day-conditional transport cost to one day's wage (dimensionless)
estimator: ratio of two independently-weighted point estimates
uncertainty_method: Nonparametric bootstrap (2,000 resamples), cost and wage populations resampled independently each draw. No cluster/PSU adjustment attempted or its absence checked for NHTS specifically.
model_counterpart: src/moments.py transport_budget_share() -- total transport spend over total effective search trips in a window, divided by the daily wage
open_audit_findings: MAJOR, QUANTIFIED (this pass): treating the 48.3% whole-block-missing group as R0 (current code) gives transport_budget_share = 0.1058, the current moments.csv value. Excluding that group from the sample entirely instead gives 0.1844 -- a 74% relative difference, holding the wage side fixed at the notebook's own R4,300 median. This dwarfs every other adjustment checked for this moment (age filter moves it by 0.3%) and is exactly the missingness-procedure decision P2.3 of the execution plan calls for (report the pattern, a defensible primary procedure, and sensitivity) -- not decided here. No design-effect/clustering check has been run for NHTS specifically.

source: Baez, J. and Kshirsagar, V. (2026). World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11285, Table 5b
version: published table (digitised from PDF page 39, not the R/Stata reproducibility package per D6)
hash: not applicable -- no microdata, digitised from the published PDF table
geography: 3 South African metros (Johannesburg, Cape Town, eThekwini), sub-place (admin-5) geography, standard errors clustered at main-place (admin-4) level -- confirmed against the paper's own Table 5b notes (Literature/baez_full.txt, page 40 of the PDF)
age_universe: CONFIRMED against the paper's own text (Literature/baez_full.txt lines 799-801): 'We present similar regressions using the share of working-age adults employed, drawn from the 2011 census (Table 5b).' Working-age is not itself defined to an exact age range in the extracted text (StatsSA's conventional 15-64 assumed, not independently confirmed).
labour_market_universe: CONFIRMED population-based, not labour-force-based: the paper's own text and Table 5b's title ('Spatial Correlates of Share of the Adult Population Employed') both describe the dependent variable as the share of the working-age POPULATION employed -- denominator is everyone working-age, not the labour force.
denominator: working-age adult population per sub-place, population-weighted (paper's own regression weights)
weights: sub-place-level population weights (paper's own specification); not applicable to this project beyond citing the paper's coefficient
missingness_treatment: not applicable (published coefficient, no microdata used by this project)
units: percentage points of employment share per 10 percentile points of within-city travel-time rank
estimator: OLS regression coefficient (paper's own specification; no population-density control per the notebook's own header note; robustness checked against a spatial-error specification with population density, per the paper's Table 5a/5b pairing)
uncertainty_method: Paper's own reported t-statistics; reconstructed per-city sampling SE = |coefficient|/|t-statistic| (Johannesburg 1.10, Cape Town 0.84, eThekwini 0.66), kept separate from moments.csv's standard_error, which is instead the cross-city sample SD (1.4048) used as a calibration-uncertainty scale, not a sampling SE
model_counterpart: src/moments.py distance_gradient_slope() -- OLS slope of EMPLOYED (share of the model's own agent/labour-force population) on percentile rank of distance_to_cbd
open_audit_findings: DECIDED 2026-09-13: removed from the fitted MSM target set (option 1 of three presented). Retained only as a QUALITATIVE external benchmark -- not described as independent quantitative validation, since it is not disjoint data collected for that purpose and the confirmed population/labour-force mismatch (verified against Literature/baez_full.txt, not just the table title: the paper's dependent variable is the working-age POPULATION employment share; the model's distance_gradient_slope() is necessarily labour-force-based) means even a directional check carries an unknown, unsigned compositional bias term. E/Pop = (E/LF)*(LF/Pop), so the paper's slope conflates the model's own estimand with however labour-force participation varies with distance -- a channel the paper does not report and no participation-by-distance profile exists to correct for. The retained (discouraged_share, transport_budget_share, long_term_share) set is now exactly identified against the 3 remaining estimated parameters -- see the bounded pre-calibration specification for the reassessed identification result.
